definition: A curved arrow with a full head that shows an electron pair moving, from a lone pair or bond to the atom or bond where the pair ends up.
A reactant that donates an electron pair to an electron-poor atom to form a new covalent bond; it can be negative, such as $\ce{OH^-}$, or neutral, such as $\ce{NH3}$.
A reactant that accepts an electron pair from a nucleophile to form a new covalent bond; it can be positive, such as $\ce{H^+}$, or neutral, such as $\ce{Br2}$.
A reaction in which a nucleophile bonds to a carbon atom and replaces a leaving group, such as a halide ion, on that carbon.
The atom or group that breaks away from a carbon atom in a substitution, taking both electrons of its old bond with it, such as $\ce{Br^-}$ from a bromoalkane.
The breaking of a covalent bond in which one fragment keeps both bonding electrons; a neutral molecule breaks into a positive ion and a negative ion.
A reaction in which an electrophile attacks the electron-rich C=C bond of an alkene and two atoms or groups add across the double bond.
